# tag: coding.cs.algorithms
what is algorithm | algorithm meaning | define algorithm | algorithm explained simply => An algorithm is a clear list of steps for solving a problem, like a recipe. Sorting a list and finding the shortest path are famous examples.
what is flowchart | flowchart meaning | define flowchart | flowchart explained simply => A flowchart draws an algorithm as boxes and arrows: ovals for start and end, rectangles for steps and diamonds for yes or no decisions.
what is big o notation | what is big o | what is time complexity | big o notation meaning | define big o notation | big o notation explained simply => Big O describes how an algorithm's work grows as the input grows. O(n) means doubling the input roughly doubles the time; O(n^2) means it roughly quadruples.
what is o(1) | what is constant time | o(1) meaning | define o(1) | o(1) explained simply => O(1), constant time, means the work stays the same no matter how big the input is, like reading `list[5]` or looking up a key in a hash table.
what is o(n) | what is linear time | o(n) meaning | define o(n) | o(n) explained simply => O(n), linear time, means the work grows in step with the input, like checking every item in a list once.
what is o(log n) | what is logarithmic time | o(log n) meaning | define o(log n) | o(log n) explained simply => O(log n) means the work grows very slowly because the problem is halved each step, like binary search: a million items need only about 20 steps.
what is o(n^2) | what is quadratic time | o(n^2) meaning | define o(n^2) | o(n^2) explained simply => O(n^2), quadratic time, happens with a loop inside a loop over the same data. 1,000 items means about a million steps, so it gets slow fast.
what is space complexity | space complexity meaning | define space complexity | space complexity explained simply => Space complexity is how much extra memory an algorithm needs as the input grows, written with Big O like time complexity.
what is linear search | linear search meaning | define linear search | linear search explained simply => Linear search checks items one by one from the start until it finds the target. It works on any list but takes O(n) time.
what is binary search | binary search meaning | define binary search | binary search explained simply => Binary search finds an item in a sorted list by checking the middle, then throwing away the half it cannot be in, again and again. It takes O(log n) time.
what is bubble sort | bubble sort meaning | define bubble sort | bubble sort explained simply => Bubble sort repeatedly swaps neighbors that are in the wrong order, so big values bubble to the end. It is easy to understand but slow, O(n^2).
what is selection sort | selection sort meaning | define selection sort | selection sort explained simply => Selection sort finds the smallest remaining item and swaps it to the front, repeating for each position. It takes O(n^2) time.
what is insertion sort | insertion sort meaning | define insertion sort | insertion sort explained simply => Insertion sort builds a sorted part one item at a time, sliding each new item back into place, like sorting cards in your hand. It is fast for nearly sorted data.
what is merge sort | merge sort meaning | define merge sort | merge sort explained simply => Merge sort splits the list in half, sorts each half, then merges the two sorted halves. It always takes O(n log n) time and keeps equal items in order.
what is quicksort | what is quick sort | quicksort meaning | define quicksort | quicksort explained simply => Quicksort picks a pivot, moves smaller items before it and bigger ones after, then sorts each side the same way. It averages O(n log n) and is very fast in practice.
what is heap sort | heap sort meaning | define heap sort | heap sort explained simply => Heap sort puts the items in a heap, then takes the largest out one at a time. It takes O(n log n) time and little extra memory.
what is counting sort | counting sort meaning | define counting sort | counting sort explained simply => Counting sort counts how many times each value appears, then writes them back in order. It is very fast when values are small whole numbers.
what is radix sort | radix sort meaning | define radix sort | radix sort explained simply => Radix sort sorts numbers digit by digit, from the last digit to the first, without comparing items directly.
what is stable sort | what is stable sorting | stable sort meaning | define stable sort | stable sort explained simply => A stable sort keeps items with equal keys in their original order, which matters when sorting by one thing after another.
what is base case | base case meaning | define base case | base case explained simply => The base case is the simplest input a recursive function answers directly without calling itself again, like factorial of 1 being 1.
what is iteration | iteration meaning | define iteration | iteration explained simply => Iteration means repeating steps with a loop, like for or while. Many recursive algorithms can be rewritten with iteration.
what is divide and conquer | divide and conquer meaning | define divide and conquer | divide and conquer explained simply => Divide and conquer splits a problem into smaller pieces, solves each, then combines the answers. Merge sort and binary search use it.
what is greedy algorithm | greedy algorithm meaning | define greedy algorithm | greedy algorithm explained simply => A greedy algorithm always makes the choice that looks best at each step. It is fast and sometimes perfect, like making change with the biggest coins first, but not always.
what is dynamic programming | dynamic programming meaning | define dynamic programming | dynamic programming explained simply => Dynamic programming solves a problem by breaking it into overlapping smaller problems and saving their answers so each is solved only once.
what is backtracking | backtracking meaning | define backtracking | backtracking explained simply => Backtracking tries choices one at a time and undoes them when they lead to a dead end, like solving a maze or a sudoku.
what is brute force | brute force meaning | define brute force | brute force explained simply => Brute force tries every possibility until one works. It is simple and correct but often too slow for big problems.
what is breadth first search | what is bfs | breadth first search meaning | define breadth first search | breadth first search explained simply => Breadth first search (BFS) explores a graph level by level using a queue. On unweighted graphs it finds the shortest path.
what is depth first search | what is dfs | depth first search meaning | define depth first search | depth first search explained simply => Depth first search (DFS) goes as far as it can down one path before backing up, using recursion or a stack. It is great for mazes and finding connected parts.
what is dijkstra's algorithm | what is dijkstra | dijkstra's algorithm meaning | define dijkstra's algorithm | dijkstra's algorithm explained simply => Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest paths from one starting point in a graph whose edges have non-negative costs, using a priority queue.
what is a star pathfinding | what is a* algorithm | a star pathfinding meaning | define a star pathfinding | a star pathfinding explained simply => A* (A star) finds a shortest path like Dijkstra but uses a guess of the distance left (a heuristic) to search toward the goal, so it is popular in games.
what is heuristic | heuristic meaning | define heuristic | heuristic explained simply => A heuristic is a smart rule of thumb or estimate that helps an algorithm decide quickly, even if it is not always perfect.
what is hashing | what is hash function | hashing meaning | define hashing | hashing explained simply => A hash function turns data into a fixed-size number. Hash tables use it to find things fast, and security uses special hash functions to check data.
what is two pointer technique | two pointer technique meaning | define two pointer technique | two pointer technique explained simply => The two pointer technique moves two indexes through a list, often from both ends toward the middle, to solve problems in O(n) instead of O(n^2).
what is sliding window | sliding window meaning | define sliding window | sliding window explained simply => A sliding window keeps a range of items and moves it along a list, adding the new item and dropping the old one, to avoid recounting everything.
what is topological sort | topological sort meaning | define topological sort | topological sort explained simply => A topological sort orders tasks so each comes after everything it depends on, like putting on socks before shoes.
what is minimum spanning tree | minimum spanning tree meaning | define minimum spanning tree | minimum spanning tree explained simply => A minimum spanning tree connects all points in a graph with the smallest total edge cost and no loops. Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms find it.
what is flood fill | flood fill meaning | define flood fill | flood fill explained simply => Flood fill spreads from a starting cell to all connected cells of the same color, like the paint bucket tool. It uses BFS or DFS.
what is euclidean algorithm | what is euclid's algorithm | euclidean algorithm meaning | define euclidean algorithm | euclidean algorithm explained simply => The Euclidean algorithm finds the greatest common divisor of two numbers by replacing the bigger one with the remainder until it reaches 0.
what is random number generator | what is rng | random number generator meaning | define random number generator | random number generator explained simply => A random number generator gives unpredictable-looking numbers. Most in programs are pseudo-random: a formula from a starting seed, so the same seed repeats the sequence.
what is seed | define seed | seed explained simply => A seed is the starting number for a pseudo-random generator. The same seed always gives the same sequence, which is how games repeat a world from a seed.
what is perlin noise | perlin noise meaning | define perlin noise | perlin noise explained simply => Perlin noise is smooth random-looking noise invented by Ken Perlin, used to make natural terrain, clouds and textures in games.
what is collision detection | collision detection meaning | define collision detection | collision detection explained simply => Collision detection checks whether game objects overlap, using simple shapes like boxes and circles first, then finer checks if needed.
what is state machine | what is finite state machine | state machine meaning | define state machine | state machine explained simply => A finite state machine is something that is always in one state, like idle, walking or jumping, and switches states when events happen. Games use them for AI and menus.
what is time complexity vs space complexity | time complexity vs space complexity meaning | define time complexity vs space complexity | time complexity vs space complexity explained simply => Time complexity is how the running time grows with input size; space complexity is how the memory use grows. Often you can trade one for the other, like caching.
what is worst case | what is worst case complexity | worst case meaning | define worst case | worst case explained simply => Worst case is the most work an algorithm can need for an input of a given size. Big O usually describes the worst case.
what is average case | average case meaning | define average case | average case explained simply => Average case is the typical amount of work over many inputs. Quicksort is O(n log n) on average but O(n^2) in its rare worst case.
what is amortized time | what is amortized complexity | amortized time meaning | define amortized time | amortized time explained simply => Amortized time is the average cost per operation over many operations. Appending to a dynamic array is amortized O(1), even though it sometimes has to grow.
what is in place algorithm | in place algorithm meaning | define in place algorithm | in place algorithm explained simply => An in-place algorithm changes the data where it is, using little extra memory, like reversing a list by swapping ends.
what is kadane's algorithm | kadane's algorithm meaning | define kadane's algorithm | kadane's algorithm explained simply => Kadane's algorithm finds the biggest sum of a run of neighbouring numbers in a list in one pass, keeping the best sum ending at each position.
what is prefix sum | what is prefix sums | prefix sum meaning | define prefix sum | prefix sum explained simply => A prefix sum array stores running totals so the sum of any range can be found instantly as `prefix[r] - prefix[l]`.
what is bit manipulation | bit manipulation meaning | define bit manipulation | bit manipulation explained simply => Bit manipulation uses operators like AND, OR, XOR and shifts on the bits of numbers, which makes some tricks very fast, like checking if a number is a power of two.
what is union find | what is disjoint set | union find meaning | union find explained simply => Union-find keeps track of which items are in the same group and can merge groups quickly. It is used to find connected parts of a graph.
what is bellman ford algorithm | what is bellman-ford | bellman ford algorithm meaning | define bellman ford algorithm | bellman ford algorithm explained simply => Bellman-Ford finds shortest paths like Dijkstra but also works when some edges have negative costs, though it is slower.
what is floyd warshall algorithm | floyd warshall algorithm meaning | define floyd warshall algorithm | floyd warshall algorithm explained simply => Floyd-Warshall finds the shortest paths between every pair of points in a graph, in O(n^3) time.
what is string matching | what is pattern search algorithm | string matching meaning | define string matching | string matching explained simply => String matching finds where a pattern appears in text. Simple checking is O(n*m), while algorithms like KMP do it in O(n + m).
what is levenshtein distance | what is edit distance | levenshtein distance meaning | define levenshtein distance | levenshtein distance explained simply => Edit distance counts the fewest single-letter inserts, deletes or changes to turn one word into another. Spell checkers use it.
what is convex hull | convex hull meaning | define convex hull | convex hull explained simply => A convex hull is the smallest convex shape containing a set of points, like a rubber band stretched around nails.
what is minimax | what is minimax algorithm | minimax meaning | define minimax | minimax explained simply => Minimax picks a move in two-player games by assuming the opponent plays their best, looking ahead through possible moves. It powers simple tic-tac-toe and chess AIs.
what is alpha beta pruning | alpha beta pruning meaning | define alpha beta pruning | alpha beta pruning explained simply => Alpha-beta pruning speeds up minimax by skipping moves that cannot change the final decision.
what is monte carlo method | what is monte carlo simulation | monte carlo method meaning | define monte carlo method | monte carlo method explained simply => Monte Carlo methods use lots of random samples to estimate an answer, like estimating pi by throwing random points at a square.
what is simulated annealing | simulated annealing meaning | define simulated annealing | simulated annealing explained simply => Simulated annealing searches for a good solution by making random changes, sometimes accepting worse ones early on to escape dead ends.
what is genetic algorithm | genetic algorithm meaning | define genetic algorithm | genetic algorithm explained simply => A genetic algorithm evolves solutions: it keeps the best of a population, mixes them and adds random mutations, over many generations.
what is cellular automaton | what is conway's game of life | cellular automaton meaning | define cellular automaton | cellular automaton explained simply => A cellular automaton is a grid of cells that change by simple rules based on their neighbours. Conway's Game of Life is the famous example.
what is raycasting | what is ray casting | raycasting meaning | define raycasting | raycasting explained simply => Raycasting sends an invisible line from a point in a direction and finds what it hits first. Games use it for shooting, line of sight and old-style 3D like Wolfenstein 3D.
what is spatial partitioning | what is quadtree | spatial partitioning meaning | define spatial partitioning | spatial partitioning explained simply => Spatial partitioning splits space into regions, like a grid or a quadtree, so a game only checks collisions between nearby objects.
what is interpolation | interpolation meaning | define interpolation | interpolation explained simply => Interpolation estimates values between known ones, like lerp for positions or smoothly blending animations.
what is hash function properties | what is good hash function | hash function properties meaning | define hash function properties | hash function properties explained simply => A good hash function is fast, gives the same output for the same input, and spreads different inputs evenly so collisions are rare.
what is checksum | checksum meaning | define checksum | checksum explained simply => A checksum is a small value calculated from data to detect accidental changes, like a damaged download.
what is load balancing | load balancing meaning | define load balancing | load balancing explained simply => Load balancing spreads work or requests across several servers so none gets overloaded.
# tag: coding.cs.data
what is data structure | data structure meaning | define data structure | data structure explained simply => A data structure is a way of organizing data so it can be used efficiently, like an array, list, stack, queue, tree or hash table.
what is array | what is arrays in programming | array meaning | define array | array explained simply => An array stores items in a row in memory, each reached by an index number. Reading any index is fast, but inserting in the middle is slow.
what is linked list | linked list meaning | define linked list | linked list explained simply => A linked list stores items in nodes, each pointing to the next one. Adding or removing in the middle is quick, but finding the 50th item means walking 50 steps.
what is stack data structure | what is stack lifo | stack data structure meaning | define stack data structure | stack data structure explained simply => A stack is last in, first out (LIFO), like a stack of plates: you push onto the top and pop from the top. Undo buttons and function calls use stacks.
what is queue data structure | what is queue fifo | queue data structure meaning | define queue data structure | queue data structure explained simply => A queue is first in, first out (FIFO), like a line at a shop: add at the back and remove from the front. It is used for tasks waiting their turn.
what is deque | deque meaning | define deque | deque explained simply => A deque (double-ended queue) lets you add and remove items at both the front and the back quickly.
what is priority queue | priority queue meaning | define priority queue | priority queue explained simply => A priority queue always gives you the item with the highest (or lowest) priority next, not the oldest. It is usually built with a heap.
what is hash table | what is hash map | hash table meaning | define hash table | hash table explained simply => A hash table stores key-value pairs and uses a hash function to jump straight to where a key lives, so lookups are about O(1) on average. Python dicts and Lua tables use them.
what is hash collision | hash collision meaning | define hash collision | hash collision explained simply => A collision is when two different keys hash to the same spot. Hash tables handle it by chaining items in a list or by probing for another slot.
what is set data structure | set data structure meaning | define set data structure | set data structure explained simply => A set holds unique items with no duplicates and can quickly tell if something is in it. Adding a value that is already there does nothing.
what is tree data structure | tree data structure meaning | define tree data structure | tree data structure explained simply => A tree is made of nodes linked parent to child, starting from one root, with no loops. Folders on a computer and Roblox's Explorer form trees.
what is binary tree | binary tree meaning | define binary tree | binary tree explained simply => A binary tree is a tree where every node has at most two children, called left and right.
what is binary search tree | what is bst | binary search tree meaning | define binary search tree | binary search tree explained simply => A binary search tree keeps smaller values in the left subtree and larger ones in the right, so searching takes O(log n) when it is balanced.
what is balanced tree | balanced tree meaning | define balanced tree | balanced tree explained simply => A balanced tree keeps its branches about the same height so operations stay O(log n). Red-black trees and AVL trees balance themselves.
what is heap data structure | what is binary heap | heap data structure meaning | define heap data structure | heap data structure explained simply => A heap is a tree where every parent is bigger (max heap) or smaller (min heap) than its children, so the top is always the largest or smallest.
what is trie | what is prefix tree | trie meaning | define trie | trie explained simply => A trie stores words letter by letter in a tree so words sharing a beginning share nodes. It is great for autocomplete.
what is graph data structure | what is graph in computer science | graph data structure meaning | define graph data structure | graph data structure explained simply => A graph is a set of nodes (vertices) connected by edges, like cities and roads or friends on a social network.
what is directed graph | directed graph meaning | define directed graph | directed graph explained simply => In a directed graph each edge has a direction, like a one-way street, so A to B does not mean B to A.
what is weighted graph | weighted graph meaning | define weighted graph | weighted graph explained simply => A weighted graph gives each edge a number, like distance or cost, which shortest path algorithms use.
what is adjacency list | adjacency list meaning | define adjacency list | adjacency list explained simply => An adjacency list stores a graph by keeping, for each node, a list of its neighbors. It uses little memory for sparse graphs.
what is adjacency matrix | adjacency matrix meaning | define adjacency matrix | adjacency matrix explained simply => An adjacency matrix stores a graph as a grid where cell [a][b] says whether a and b are connected. Checking an edge is instant but it uses n^2 memory.
what is node | node meaning | define node | node explained simply => A node is one item in a linked structure like a list, tree or graph, holding a value and links to other nodes.
what is pointer in computer science | what is memory address | pointer in computer science meaning | define pointer in computer science | pointer in computer science explained simply => A pointer is a value that holds a memory address, telling where other data lives. Languages like C and C++ let you use them directly.
what is matrix | what is 2d array | matrix meaning | matrix explained simply => A matrix or 2D array is a grid of values in rows and columns, read with two indexes like `grid[row][col]`. Game boards and images are often stored this way.
what is tuple | tuple meaning | define tuple | tuple explained simply => A tuple is a small fixed group of values kept together, like (x, y). In Python tuples cannot be changed after they are made.
what is record | what is struct in computer science | record explained simply => A record, or struct, groups named fields together, like a player's name, health and score.
what is immutable | immutable meaning | define immutable | immutable explained simply => Immutable means it cannot be changed after it is created. To change it, you make a new one. Python strings and tuples are immutable.
what is mutable | mutable meaning | define mutable | mutable explained simply => Mutable means it can be changed in place, like a Python list or a Lua table.
what is index | index meaning | define index | index explained simply => An index is the position number of an item. Most languages start counting at 0, but Lua and Luau start at 1.
what is zero based indexing | why do arrays start at 0 | zero based indexing meaning | define zero based indexing | zero based indexing explained simply => Zero-based indexing means the first item is at index 0. It comes from the index being the offset from the start of the array in memory.
what is serialization | serialization meaning | define serialization | serialization explained simply => Serialization turns data in memory into text or bytes, like JSON, so it can be saved or sent. Deserialization turns it back.
what is cache | cache meaning | define cache | cache explained simply => A cache keeps copies of data that is slow to get, so asking again is fast. CPUs, browsers and apps all use caches.
what is buffer | buffer meaning | define buffer | buffer explained simply => A buffer is a chunk of memory that temporarily holds data while it moves between places, like audio waiting to play.
what is linked list vs array | linked list vs array meaning | define linked list vs array | linked list vs array explained simply => Arrays are fast to index and use memory well; linked lists are fast to insert into the middle but slow to index. Most of the time arrays (lists) win.
what is circular buffer | what is ring buffer | circular buffer meaning | define circular buffer | circular buffer explained simply => A circular buffer is a fixed-size array that wraps around when it reaches the end, great for keeping the last N readings or audio samples.
what is sparse array | what is sparse matrix | sparse array meaning | define sparse array | sparse array explained simply => A sparse array is mostly empty, so it is stored as a list or dictionary of only the filled positions to save memory.
what is bloom filter | bloom filter meaning | define bloom filter | bloom filter explained simply => A Bloom filter quickly tells you an item is definitely not in a set or maybe is, using very little memory.
what is skip list | skip list meaning | define skip list | skip list explained simply => A skip list is a linked list with extra express lanes that skip ahead, giving fast search like a balanced tree.
what is b-tree | what is b tree | b-tree meaning | define b-tree | b-tree explained simply => A B-tree is a balanced tree whose nodes hold many keys, designed for databases and file systems that read from disk in blocks.
what is red black tree | red black tree meaning | define red black tree | red black tree explained simply => A red-black tree is a self-balancing binary search tree that colors nodes to keep its height low. C++ std::map is usually one.
what is avl tree | avl tree meaning | define avl tree | avl tree explained simply => An AVL tree is a binary search tree that rebalances itself after every change so its height stays about log n.
what is segment tree | segment tree meaning | define segment tree | segment tree explained simply => A segment tree answers range questions, like the sum or minimum of part of an array, and handles updates, both in O(log n).
what is graph cycle | what is cycle in a graph | graph cycle meaning | define graph cycle | graph cycle explained simply => A cycle is a path in a graph that comes back to where it started. Trees have no cycles.
what is dag | what is directed acyclic graph | dag meaning | define dag | dag explained simply => A directed acyclic graph has one-way edges and no cycles, like a task list where some tasks must come before others. Git history is a DAG.
what is string encoding | string encoding meaning | define string encoding | string encoding explained simply => String encoding is how characters are turned into bytes. UTF-8 is the common choice; opening a file with the wrong encoding shows garbled text.
what is base64 | base64 meaning | define base64 | base64 explained simply => Base64 turns any bytes into plain letters, digits, + and /, so binary data like images can travel inside text such as JSON or email. It is not encryption.
what is uuid | what is guid | uuid meaning | define uuid | uuid explained simply => A UUID (or GUID) is a 128-bit ID made so that two random ones will practically never be the same, used to label things without a central counter.
what is timestamp | what is unix time | timestamp meaning | define timestamp | timestamp explained simply => A Unix timestamp counts seconds since 1 January 1970 UTC. It is an easy way to store and compare times.
what is data compression ratio | data compression ratio meaning | define data compression ratio | data compression ratio explained simply => The compression ratio compares the original size to the compressed size. Text compresses well; already compressed files like JPGs barely shrink.
what is metadata | metadata explained simply => Metadata is data about data, like a photo's date and camera, or a file's size and creation time.
what is schema | schema meaning | define schema | schema explained simply => A schema describes the shape of data, like which fields a database table or JSON object must have and their types.
what is normalization in databases | what is database normalization | normalization in databases meaning | define normalization in databases | normalization in databases explained simply => Normalization organizes a database so each fact is stored in one place, avoiding repeated data that can get out of sync.
what is nosql | nosql meaning | define nosql | nosql explained simply => NoSQL databases store data in forms other than tables, like documents or key-value pairs. Roblox DataStores work like a key-value store.
what is key value store | key value store meaning | define key value store | key value store explained simply => A key-value store saves values under keys, like a giant dictionary. It is simple and fast; Roblox DataStores and Redis work this way.
what is index in databases | what is database index | index in databases meaning | define index in databases | index in databases explained simply => A database index is like a book's index: it lets the database find rows by a column quickly instead of checking every row.
# tag: coding.cs.computers
what is bit | bit explained simply => A bit is the smallest piece of computer data, a single 0 or 1.
what is byte | byte meaning | define byte | byte explained simply => A byte is 8 bits, enough to store a number from 0 to 255 or one basic character like 'A'.
what is kilobyte megabyte gigabyte | what is data sizes | kilobyte megabyte gigabyte meaning | define kilobyte megabyte gigabyte | kilobyte megabyte gigabyte explained simply => Each step is about a thousand times bigger: kilobyte (KB), megabyte (MB), gigabyte (GB), terabyte (TB). Strictly a KiB is 1,024 bytes and a KB is 1,000.
what is hexadecimal | what is hex numbers | hexadecimal meaning | define hexadecimal | hexadecimal explained simply => Hexadecimal is base 16, using 0-9 and A-F. One hex digit is exactly 4 bits, so colors like #FF8800 and memory addresses are often written in hex.
what is octal | octal meaning | define octal | octal explained simply => Octal is base 8, using digits 0 to 7. It is mostly seen in Unix file permissions like 755.
what is two's complement | two's complement meaning | define two's complement | two's complement explained simply => Two's complement is how computers store negative whole numbers: flip all the bits and add 1. It lets the same adding circuit handle negatives.
what is integer overflow | what is overflow in computing | integer overflow meaning | define integer overflow | integer overflow explained simply => Overflow happens when a number gets too big for its storage and wraps around or breaks, like an 8-bit counter going from 255 back to 0.
what is floating point | floating point meaning | define floating point | floating point explained simply => Floating point stores decimals in binary like scientific notation. Many decimals, like 0.1, cannot be exact, so tiny rounding errors appear.
what is ascii | ascii meaning | define ascii | ascii explained simply => ASCII is an old code that gives 128 characters a number, like 65 for 'A' and 97 for 'a'. It covers English letters, digits and symbols.
what is unicode | unicode meaning | define unicode | unicode explained simply => Unicode gives a number to almost every character in every language, plus emoji, so text works worldwide.
what is utf-8 | utf-8 meaning | define utf-8 | utf-8 explained simply => UTF-8 is the most common way to store Unicode text. English letters take 1 byte and other characters take 2 to 4, and it matches ASCII for basic text.
what is cpu | what is processor | cpu meaning | define cpu | cpu explained simply => The CPU (central processing unit) is the brain of a computer that runs instructions one after another, billions of times a second.
what is gpu | what is graphics card | gpu meaning | define gpu | gpu explained simply => A GPU has thousands of small cores that do many calculations at once, perfect for drawing 3D graphics and for AI.
what is register in a cpu | what is cpu register | register in a cpu meaning | define register in a cpu | register in a cpu explained simply => Registers are the CPU's own handful of tiny storage slots that hold the values it is working on at that instant.
what is fetch decode execute cycle | fetch decode execute cycle meaning | define fetch decode execute cycle | fetch decode execute cycle explained simply => The CPU repeats three steps: fetch the next instruction from memory, decode what it means, then execute it.
what is von neumann architecture | von neumann architecture meaning | define von neumann architecture | von neumann architecture explained simply => Von Neumann architecture is the design most computers use, where programs and data are stored in the same memory and a CPU runs instructions from it.
what is machine code | machine code meaning | define machine code | machine code explained simply => Machine code is the binary instructions a CPU actually runs. Compilers turn your code into it.
what is assembly language | assembly language meaning | define assembly language | assembly language explained simply => Assembly is a low-level language with one short word for each CPU instruction, like MOV and ADD. An assembler turns it into machine code.
what is compiler | compiler meaning | define compiler | compiler explained simply => A compiler translates a whole program into machine code (or another form) before it runs. C++, Rust and Swift are compiled.
what is interpreter | interpreter meaning | define interpreter | interpreter explained simply => An interpreter runs code more or less line by line without making a separate program first. Python is usually interpreted.
what is bytecode | bytecode meaning | define bytecode | bytecode explained simply => Bytecode is a compact in-between form of code that a virtual machine runs, like Java's .class files or Python's .pyc files.
what is virtual machine in programming | what is vm | virtual machine in programming meaning | define virtual machine in programming | virtual machine in programming explained simply => A virtual machine is software that pretends to be a computer, either to run bytecode like the Java VM or to run a whole operating system.
what is jit compiler | what is just in time compilation | jit compiler meaning | define jit compiler | jit compiler explained simply => A just-in-time (JIT) compiler turns code into machine code while the program runs, speeding up hot parts. JavaScript engines use it.
what is garbage collection | garbage collection meaning | define garbage collection | garbage collection explained simply => Garbage collection automatically frees memory that the program can no longer reach, so you do not have to. Python, Lua, Java and JavaScript use it.
what is kernel | kernel meaning | define kernel | kernel explained simply => The kernel is the core of an operating system that controls memory, the CPU and devices, and decides which program runs when.
what is process | process meaning | define process | process explained simply => A process is a running program with its own memory. Opening an app starts a process.
what is thread | thread meaning | define thread | thread explained simply => A thread is one path of execution inside a process. A process can have many threads sharing its memory, doing work at the same time.
what is file system | file system meaning | define file system | file system explained simply => A file system organizes files and folders on a drive and tracks where each one is stored.
what is logic gate | what is logic gates | logic gate meaning | define logic gate | logic gate explained simply => Logic gates are tiny circuits that take bits in and give a bit out. AND, OR and NOT gates combined make every part of a computer.
what is and gate | and gate meaning | define and gate | and gate explained simply => An AND gate outputs 1 only when both inputs are 1.
what is not gate | not gate meaning | define not gate | not gate explained simply => A NOT gate flips its input: 1 becomes 0 and 0 becomes 1.
what is xor gate | what is exclusive or | xor gate meaning | define xor gate | xor gate explained simply => XOR (exclusive or) outputs 1 when the inputs are different and 0 when they are the same.
what is nand gate | nand gate meaning | define nand gate | nand gate explained simply => A NAND gate is an AND gate followed by NOT. Every other gate can be built from NAND gates alone.
what is boolean logic | what is boolean algebra | boolean logic meaning | define boolean logic | boolean logic explained simply => Boolean logic works with true and false using AND, OR and NOT. It is the math behind if statements and logic gates.
what is transistor in computers | transistor in computers meaning | define transistor in computers | transistor in computers explained simply => A transistor is a tiny electronic switch. Modern chips contain billions of them, combined into logic gates.
what is turing machine | turing machine meaning | define turing machine | turing machine explained simply => A Turing machine is Alan Turing's simple imaginary computer: a tape of symbols and a head following rules. It defines what can be computed at all.
what is turing complete | turing complete meaning | define turing complete | turing complete explained simply => A language or system is Turing complete if it can compute anything a Turing machine can, given enough time and memory. Most programming languages are, and so is Minecraft redstone.
what is halting problem | halting problem meaning | define halting problem | halting problem explained simply => The halting problem, proved by Alan Turing in 1936, shows no program can always correctly decide whether any other program will eventually stop or run forever.
what is p vs np | p vs np meaning | define p vs np | p vs np explained simply => P vs NP asks whether every problem whose answer can be checked quickly can also be solved quickly. It is a famous unsolved problem with a million dollar prize.
what is first computer bug | why is it called a bug | first computer bug meaning | define first computer bug | first computer bug explained simply => In 1947 engineers working on the Harvard Mark II found a real moth stuck in a relay and taped it in their logbook as the "first actual case of bug being found".
what is emulator | emulator meaning | define emulator | emulator explained simply => An emulator is software that copies how another device works, so you can run its programs, like an old console's games on a PC.
what is driver | driver meaning | define driver | driver explained simply => A driver is software that lets the operating system talk to a piece of hardware, like a printer or graphics card.
what is bios | bios meaning | define bios | bios explained simply => BIOS or UEFI is the firmware that starts a computer, checks the hardware and loads the operating system.
what is pixel | pixel meaning | define pixel | pixel explained simply => A pixel is one tiny dot of color on a screen or in an image. A 1920x1080 screen has about 2 million of them.
what is raster vs vector graphics | what is vector graphics | raster vs vector graphics meaning | define raster vs vector graphics | raster vs vector graphics explained simply => Raster images, like PNG and JPG, are grids of pixels and get blocky when enlarged. Vector images, like SVG, store shapes and stay sharp at any size.
what is frame rate | frame rate meaning | define frame rate | frame rate explained simply => Frame rate, in frames per second (FPS), is how many images a game draws each second. 60 FPS looks smooth; each frame then gets about 16.7 ms.
what is rendering | rendering meaning | define rendering | rendering explained simply => Rendering is the computer drawing an image from a scene's shapes, materials and lights. Games render many frames every second.
what is shader | shader meaning | define shader | shader explained simply => A shader is a small program that runs on the GPU to decide the color of pixels or the position of vertices, creating effects like lighting and water.
what is polygon | what is mesh in 3d | polygon meaning | polygon explained simply => Models in 3D are meshes made of many flat polygons, usually triangles. More triangles look smoother but cost more to draw.
what is sampling rate | what is audio sample rate | sampling rate meaning | define sampling rate | sampling rate explained simply => Digital audio measures the sound wave many times a second; 44,100 samples per second is CD quality.
what is boolean expression | boolean expression meaning | define boolean expression | boolean expression explained simply => A boolean expression gives true or false, like `score > 10 and lives > 0`.
what is instruction set | what is isa | instruction set meaning | define instruction set | instruction set explained simply => An instruction set architecture lists the instructions a CPU understands. x86-64 is in most PCs, and ARM is in phones, tablets and Apple silicon Macs.
what is arm processor | what is arm chips | arm processor meaning | define arm processor | arm processor explained simply => ARM chips are energy-efficient processors used in nearly all phones and tablets, Apple silicon Macs and many microcontrollers.
what is x86 | x86 meaning | define x86 | x86 explained simply => The x86 family (and its 64-bit form x86-64) is the processor type in most Windows PCs, made by Intel and AMD.
what is bus in computers | what is data bus | bus in computers meaning | define bus in computers | bus in computers explained simply => A bus is the set of wires that carries data between parts of a computer, like between the CPU and memory.
what is interrupt in computing | what is hardware interrupt | interrupt in computing meaning | define interrupt in computing | interrupt in computing explained simply => An interrupt is a signal that makes the CPU pause what it is doing to handle something urgent, like a key press, then carry on.
what is virtual memory | virtual memory meaning | define virtual memory | virtual memory explained simply => Virtual memory gives each program its own pretend address space and can move rarely used data to the disk when RAM is full.
what is paging | what is swap file | paging meaning | define paging | paging explained simply => When RAM is full, the operating system moves some memory pages to disk (swap). Disk is much slower, so heavy swapping makes a computer crawl.
what is context switch | context switch meaning | define context switch | context switch explained simply => A context switch is when the CPU saves one task's state and loads another's so many programs can share the CPU.
what is scheduler | what is cpu scheduler | scheduler meaning | define scheduler | scheduler explained simply => The scheduler is the part of the operating system that decides which thread runs on which CPU core and for how long.
what is bootloader | bootloader meaning | define bootloader | bootloader explained simply => A bootloader is a small program that runs when a device starts and loads the main operating system or program.
what is endianness in computers | what is byte order in computers | endianness in computers meaning | define endianness in computers | endianness in computers explained simply => Endianness is the order bytes of a number are stored in. Little-endian puts the smallest byte first and is used by most modern chips.
what is floating point unit | what is fpu | floating point unit meaning | define floating point unit | floating point unit explained simply => An FPU is the part of a processor that does decimal (floating point) math in hardware. Small microcontrollers without one do it slowly in software.
what is benchmark score | what is benchmarks for computers | benchmark score meaning | define benchmark score | benchmark score explained simply => A benchmark runs a standard test so you can compare the speed of different devices fairly.
what is codec | codec meaning | define codec | codec explained simply => A codec compresses and decompresses audio or video, like H.264, HEVC, AV1 or AAC.
what is aliasing | what is anti-aliasing | aliasing meaning | define aliasing | aliasing explained simply => Aliasing makes jagged stair-step edges on diagonal lines. Anti-aliasing smooths them by blending edge pixels.
what is texture in 3d graphics | what is texture mapping | texture in 3d graphics meaning | define texture in 3d graphics | texture in 3d graphics explained simply => A texture is an image wrapped onto a 3D model's surface to give it color and detail.
what is frame buffer | what is framebuffer | frame buffer meaning | define frame buffer | frame buffer explained simply => The framebuffer is the memory holding the image about to be shown on screen.
what is v-sync | what is vsync | v-sync meaning | define v-sync | v-sync explained simply => V-sync makes a game wait for the screen to finish showing a frame before swapping, preventing screen tearing but sometimes adding a little delay.
# tag: coding.cs.programming
what is programming language | programming language meaning | define programming language | programming language explained simply => A programming language is a set of words and rules for writing instructions a computer can run, like Python, Luau, Swift or C++.
what is syntax | syntax meaning | syntax explained simply => Syntax is the grammar rules of a programming language, like where brackets and commas go. Breaking them gives a syntax error.
what is semantics | semantics explained simply => Semantics is what code actually means and does when it runs, as opposed to syntax, which is how it is written.
what is high level language | high level language meaning | define high level language | high level language explained simply => A high-level language, like Python or Luau, is close to human language and hides hardware details. Low-level languages like assembly are close to the machine.
what is low level language | low level language meaning | define low level language | low level language explained simply => A low-level language, like assembly or C, gives close control over the hardware and memory, with fewer helpers.
what is variable | variable meaning | define variable | variable explained simply => A variable is a named box that stores a value your program can read and change, like `score = 10`.
what is constant | constant meaning | define constant | constant explained simply => A constant is a named value that should not change while the program runs, like the maximum number of players.
what is integer | integer meaning | integer explained simply => An integer is a whole number with no decimal part, like -3, 0 or 42.
what is float | what is floating point number | float meaning | define float | float explained simply => A float is a number with a decimal point, like 3.14. Floats can have tiny rounding errors.
what is string | string meaning | define string | string explained simply => A string is a piece of text, a sequence of characters, usually written in quotes like "hello".
what is boolean | boolean meaning | define boolean | boolean explained simply => A boolean is a value that is either true or false, named after the mathematician George Boole.
what is null | what is nil | what is none | null meaning | define null | null explained simply => Null means no value at all. Different languages name it null, nil (Lua, Swift) or None (Python).
what is operator | operator meaning | define operator | operator explained simply => An operator is a symbol that does something with values, like + to add, == to compare or and to combine conditions.
what is expression | expression meaning | define expression | expression explained simply => An expression is code that produces a value, like `2 + 3` or `health > 0`.
what is statement | statement meaning | statement explained simply => A statement is a complete instruction, like an assignment, an if or a loop. Expressions make values; statements do things.
what is conditional | what is if statement | conditional meaning | define conditional | conditional explained simply => A conditional runs code only when something is true: if this, do that, else do something else.
what is loop | loop meaning | define loop | loop explained simply => A loop repeats code. A for loop repeats a set number of times or over a list; a while loop repeats as long as a condition is true.
what is function | function meaning | function explained simply => A function is a named, reusable block of code that can take inputs (parameters) and give back an output (return value).
what is parameter vs argument | what is parameter and argument | parameter vs argument meaning | define parameter vs argument | parameter vs argument explained simply => A parameter is the name in a function's definition, like `x` in `def double(x)`. An argument is the actual value you pass in, like 5 in `double(5)`.
what is return value | return value meaning | define return value | return value explained simply => A return value is what a function hands back to the code that called it.
what is scope | scope meaning | define scope | scope explained simply => Scope is the part of the code where a variable exists. A variable made inside a function usually cannot be seen outside it.
what is global variable | global variable meaning | define global variable | global variable explained simply => A global variable can be used anywhere in the program. Too many make code hard to follow because anything can change them.
what is local variable | local variable meaning | define local variable | local variable explained simply => A local variable only exists inside the block or function where it was made, which keeps code tidy and safer.
what is closure | closure meaning | define closure | closure explained simply => A closure is a function that remembers variables from the place it was created, even after that code has finished running.
what is callback | callback meaning | define callback | callback explained simply => A callback is a function you pass to other code so it can call it later, like when a button is clicked or a download finishes.
what is event driven programming | what is events in programming | event driven programming meaning | define event driven programming | event driven programming explained simply => In event-driven programming, code runs in response to events, like clicks, key presses or a player touching a part, instead of in one fixed order.
what is library | library meaning | define library | library explained simply => A library is a collection of ready-made code you can use in your program instead of writing it yourself.
what is framework | framework meaning | define framework | framework explained simply => A framework is a bigger structure you build your app inside, like SwiftUI or React, that calls your code at the right times.
what is api | api meaning | define api | api explained simply => An API (application programming interface) is a set of functions or web addresses that lets one program use another's features or data.
what is sdk | sdk meaning | define sdk | sdk explained simply => An SDK (software development kit) is a bundle of tools, libraries and docs for making software for a platform, like the iOS SDK.
what is ide | ide meaning | define ide | ide explained simply => An IDE (integrated development environment) is an app for coding that combines an editor, running and debugging, like Xcode, Visual Studio or Roblox Studio.
what is source code | source code meaning | define source code | source code explained simply => Source code is the human-readable code programmers write, before it is compiled or run.
what is bug | bug meaning | define bug | bug explained simply => A bug is a mistake in a program that makes it do the wrong thing or crash.
what is runtime error | runtime error meaning | define runtime error | runtime error explained simply => A runtime error happens while the program is running, like dividing by zero or using a value that is nil.
what is logic error | logic error meaning | define logic error | logic error explained simply => A logic error means the code runs without crashing but gives the wrong result, because the steps themselves are wrong.
what is breakpoint | breakpoint meaning | define breakpoint | breakpoint explained simply => A breakpoint pauses a program at a chosen line so you can inspect variables and step through the code in a debugger.
what is stack trace | what is traceback | stack trace meaning | define stack trace | stack trace explained simply => A stack trace lists the chain of function calls that led to an error, with file names and line numbers, so you can find where it went wrong.
what is rubber duck debugging | rubber duck debugging meaning | define rubber duck debugging | rubber duck debugging explained simply => Rubber duck debugging means explaining your code line by line to a rubber duck (or anyone). Saying it out loud often reveals the bug.
what is edge case | edge case meaning | define edge case | edge case explained simply => An edge case is an unusual input at the limits, like an empty list, zero or a huge number, where bugs often hide.
what is unit test | unit test meaning | define unit test | unit test explained simply => A unit test is a small automatic check that one piece of code, like a function, gives the right answer.
what is test driven development | what is tdd | test driven development meaning | define test driven development | test driven development explained simply => Test-driven development means writing a failing test first, then writing just enough code to pass it, then cleaning up.
what is refactoring | refactoring meaning | define refactoring | refactoring explained simply => Refactoring is improving how code is written, making it cleaner or simpler, without changing what it does.
what is technical debt | what is tech debt | technical debt meaning | define technical debt | technical debt explained simply => Technical debt is the extra work you create later by taking shortcuts now, like messy code that becomes hard to change.
what is dry principle | what is dont repeat yourself | dry principle meaning | define dry principle | dry principle explained simply => DRY means Don't Repeat Yourself: if you copy the same code around, put it in a function or module so a fix only happens once.
what is kiss principle | kiss principle meaning | define kiss principle | kiss principle explained simply => KISS means Keep It Simple: the simplest solution that works is usually easiest to understand and fix.
what is spaghetti code | spaghetti code meaning | define spaghetti code | spaghetti code explained simply => Spaghetti code is tangled code that jumps around and is hard to follow. Functions, modules and clear names untangle it.
what is magic number | magic number meaning | define magic number | magic number explained simply => A magic number is an unexplained number in code, like `if speed > 37`. Give it a named constant so readers know what it means.
what is naming conventions | what is camelcase vs snake_case | naming conventions meaning | define naming conventions | naming conventions explained simply => The camelCase style (Luau, Swift, JavaScript) joins words with capitals, snake_case (Python) uses underscores, and PascalCase capitalizes every word for classes and types.
what is hard coding | hard coding meaning | define hard coding | hard coding explained simply => Hard coding means putting fixed values straight into code instead of reading them from settings or data, which makes changes harder later.
what is modular programming | what is modules in programming | modular programming meaning | define modular programming | modular programming explained simply => Modular programming splits a program into separate pieces, like ModuleScripts or Python modules, each with one job.
what is class | class meaning | define class | class explained simply => A class is a blueprint for making objects, describing what data they hold and what they can do.
what is object | what is instance | object meaning | define object | object explained simply => An object, or instance, is one thing made from a class, with its own values, like one particular enemy made from the Enemy class.
what is method | method meaning | define method | method explained simply => A method is a function that belongs to an object or class, like `player:Kick()` or `list.append(5)`.
what is inheritance | inheritance meaning | define inheritance | inheritance explained simply => Inheritance lets a class get the data and methods of another class and add its own, like Boss inheriting from Enemy.
what is polymorphism | polymorphism meaning | define polymorphism | polymorphism explained simply => Polymorphism means different types can be used through the same interface, each doing its own version, like every shape having its own draw method.
what is encapsulation | encapsulation meaning | define encapsulation | encapsulation explained simply => Encapsulation keeps an object's data private and only lets other code change it through its methods, so it cannot be put in a broken state.
what is abstraction | abstraction meaning | define abstraction | abstraction explained simply => Abstraction hides complicated details behind a simple interface, like pressing a button without knowing the wiring inside.
what is interface | what is protocol in programming | interface meaning | define interface | interface explained simply => An interface (called a protocol in Swift) is a list of methods a type promises to have, without saying how they work.
what is functional programming | functional programming meaning | define functional programming | functional programming explained simply => Functional programming builds programs from functions that avoid changing state, often using map, filter and reduce.
what is side effect | side effect meaning | define side effect | side effect explained simply => A side effect is anything a function does besides returning a value, like printing, changing a global or saving a file.
what is higher order function | higher order function meaning | define higher order function | higher order function explained simply => A higher-order function takes functions as arguments or returns one, like map, filter and sort with a comparison function.
what is map filter reduce | map filter reduce meaning | define map filter reduce | map filter reduce explained simply => The map step changes every item, filter keeps items that pass a test, and reduce combines all items into one value, like a total.
what is lambda | what is anonymous function | lambda meaning | define lambda | lambda explained simply => A lambda is a small function without a name, written inline, like `lambda x: x * 2` in Python.
what is static typing | static typing meaning | define static typing | static typing explained simply => In static typing, variable types are checked before the program runs, as in Swift, C++ and typed Luau. Mistakes are caught early.
what is dynamic typing | dynamic typing meaning | define dynamic typing | dynamic typing explained simply => In dynamic typing, types are checked while the program runs and a variable can hold any type, as in Python, Lua and JavaScript.
what is type inference | type inference meaning | define type inference | type inference explained simply => Type inference means the compiler works out a variable's type from its value, so you can write `let x = 5` in Swift without saying Int.
what is type casting | what is type conversion | type casting meaning | define type casting | type casting explained simply => Type conversion turns a value into another type, like the text "42" into the number 42.
what is concurrency | concurrency meaning | define concurrency | concurrency explained simply => Concurrency is a program handling several tasks during the same period, switching between them, like downloading while the UI stays responsive.
what is parallelism | parallelism meaning | define parallelism | parallelism explained simply => Parallelism means truly doing several things at the exact same time on different CPU cores.
what is asynchronous programming | what is async | asynchronous programming meaning | define asynchronous programming | asynchronous programming explained simply => Asynchronous code starts a slow task, like loading from the internet, and keeps going instead of freezing while it waits for the result.
what is race condition | race condition meaning | define race condition | race condition explained simply => A race condition is a bug where the result depends on which of two things happening at once finishes first, like two scripts changing the same value.
what is deadlock | deadlock meaning | define deadlock | deadlock explained simply => A deadlock is when two tasks each wait for the other to let go of something, so both wait forever.
what is regular expression | what is regex | regular expression meaning | define regular expression | regular expression explained simply => A regular expression is a pattern for matching text, like `\d+` for one or more digits. Lua and Luau use their own simpler string patterns instead.
what is recursion vs iteration | recursion vs iteration meaning | define recursion vs iteration | recursion vs iteration explained simply => Recursion solves a problem by a function calling itself; iteration uses loops. Recursion can be clearer for trees, while loops use less memory.
what is software development life cycle | what is sdlc | software development life cycle meaning | define software development life cycle | software development life cycle explained simply => The software development life cycle goes from planning and design to coding, testing, releasing and maintaining software.
what is agile | agile meaning | define agile | agile explained simply => Agile is a way of building software in short cycles called sprints, showing working pieces often and adjusting from feedback.
what is mvp | what is minimum viable product | mvp meaning | define mvp | mvp explained simply => A minimum viable product is the smallest version of an idea that people can actually use, built first to test whether the idea works.
what is version control | version control meaning | define version control | version control explained simply => Version control, like Git, keeps a history of every change to your code so you can go back, compare versions and work with others.
what is software license | software license meaning | define software license | software license explained simply => A software license says what others may do with code. MIT is very permissive, while GPL requires shared changes to stay open source.
what is documentation | documentation meaning | define documentation | documentation explained simply => Documentation explains how code or a tool works and how to use it, through comments, READMEs or reference pages.
what is dependency | dependency meaning | define dependency | dependency explained simply => A dependency is outside code your project needs to run, like a library or package.
what is package manager | package manager meaning | define package manager | package manager explained simply => A package manager installs and updates libraries for you, like pip for Python, npm for JavaScript, Swift Package Manager or Wally for Roblox.
what is build | build meaning | define build | build explained simply => A build turns source code into a runnable app, including compiling, linking and packaging.
what is deployment | what is deploy | deployment meaning | define deployment | deployment explained simply => Deploying means putting a new version of software where people use it, like publishing a game or releasing an app.
what is full stack | full stack meaning | define full stack | full stack explained simply => A full-stack developer works on both the frontend (what users see) and the backend (servers and databases).
what is client server model | what is client and server | client server model meaning | define client server model | client server model explained simply => In the client-server model, clients like your browser or Roblox app ask a server for things, and the server answers. Roblox games run code on both sides.
what is bot | bot meaning | define bot | bot explained simply => A bot is a program that does tasks automatically, like a Discord bot that answers commands.
what is imperative programming | imperative programming meaning | define imperative programming | imperative programming explained simply => Imperative programming tells the computer step by step how to do something, with statements that change variables.
what is declarative programming | declarative programming meaning | define declarative programming | declarative programming explained simply => Declarative programming describes what you want rather than how to do it, like SQL queries, HTML or SwiftUI layouts.
what is procedural programming | procedural programming meaning | define procedural programming | procedural programming explained simply => Procedural programming organizes code into procedures (functions) that run in order, like most beginner programs in Python or Lua.
what is compiled vs interpreted | what is compiled vs interpreted language | compiled vs interpreted meaning | define compiled vs interpreted | compiled vs interpreted explained simply => A compiled language is translated to machine code before running, which is usually faster. An interpreted language is run by another program as it goes, which is easier to change and test.
what is strongly typed | strongly typed meaning | define strongly typed | strongly typed explained simply => A strongly typed language refuses to mix types silently, like Python refusing to add a string and a number. Weakly typed languages, like JavaScript, convert automatically.
what is first class functions | first class functions meaning | define first class functions | first class functions explained simply => A language has first-class functions when functions are values you can store in variables, pass to other functions and return. Lua, Python, Swift and JavaScript all do.
what is recursion depth | what is maximum recursion depth | recursion depth meaning | define recursion depth | recursion depth explained simply => Recursion depth is how many calls deep a recursive function goes. Too deep and you run out of stack; Python stops at about 1000 by default.
what is immutability | immutability meaning | define immutability | immutability explained simply => Immutability means values never change after they are made; you create new ones instead. It makes code easier to reason about, especially with threads.
what is generics in programming | what is generic programming | generics in programming meaning | define generics in programming | generics in programming explained simply => Generics let you write code once that works with many types, like a list of any type, while still checking types. Swift, C++ (templates) and typed Luau have them.
what is operator overloading | operator overloading meaning | define operator overloading | operator overloading explained simply => Operator overloading lets your own types work with symbols like + and ==, such as adding two Vector3 values in Roblox.
what is reflection in programming | reflection in programming meaning | define reflection in programming | reflection in programming explained simply => Reflection lets a program look at its own types, properties and methods while it runs.
what is dependency injection in programming | dependency injection in programming meaning | define dependency injection in programming | dependency injection in programming explained simply => Dependency injection means giving an object the things it needs from outside instead of it creating them, which makes testing easier.
what is coupling and cohesion | coupling and cohesion meaning | define coupling and cohesion | coupling and cohesion explained simply => Low coupling means parts depend on each other as little as possible; high cohesion means each part does one focused job. Both make code easier to change.
what is solid principles | solid principles meaning | define solid principles | solid principles explained simply => SOLID is five object-oriented design rules: single responsibility, open/closed, Liskov substitution, interface segregation and dependency inversion.
what is yagni | yagni meaning | define yagni | yagni explained simply => YAGNI means You Aren't Gonna Need It: do not build features until you actually need them.
what is code smell | code smell meaning | define code smell | code smell explained simply => A code smell is a sign something may be wrong in code, like a huge function, repeated code or a confusing name.
what is boilerplate code | boilerplate code meaning | define boilerplate code | boilerplate code explained simply => Boilerplate is repetitive setup code you need to write over and over with little change, which frameworks and snippets try to reduce.
what is linting | what is linter in programming | linting meaning | define linting | linting explained simply => A linter checks code for likely mistakes and style issues without running it, like Selene for Luau or Ruff for Python.
what is code formatter | what is auto formatter | code formatter meaning | define code formatter | code formatter explained simply => A formatter rewrites code into a consistent style automatically, like StyLua for Luau, Black or Ruff for Python, and Prettier for JavaScript.
what is static analysis | static analysis meaning | define static analysis | static analysis explained simply => Static analysis checks code for bugs without running it, like type checkers and linters do.
what is integration test | integration test meaning | define integration test | integration test explained simply => An integration test checks that several parts of a program work together correctly, not just one function alone.
what is regression | what is regression bug | regression meaning | define regression | regression explained simply => A regression is a bug where something that used to work breaks after a change. Automated tests catch regressions early.
what is code coverage | code coverage meaning | define code coverage | code coverage explained simply => Code coverage measures how much of your code is run by your tests. High coverage helps but does not prove the code is correct.
what is mock object | what is mocking | mock object meaning | define mock object | mock object explained simply => A mock is a fake version of something, like a fake server, used in tests so they run fast and predictably.
what is hotfix in software | hotfix in software meaning | define hotfix in software | hotfix in software explained simply => A hotfix is a quick, small fix for an urgent bug in software people are already using.
what is end of life | what is eol software | end of life meaning | define end of life | end of life explained simply => End of life means a product no longer gets updates or security fixes, so it becomes risky to keep using.
what is deprecated | what is deprecation | deprecated meaning | define deprecated | deprecated explained simply => Deprecated means a feature still works but is being phased out, so you should switch to the newer replacement before it is removed.
what is breaking change in software | breaking change in software meaning | define breaking change in software | breaking change in software explained simply => A breaking change is an update that makes existing code or files stop working, so users must change things to upgrade.
what is api documentation | what is api docs | api documentation meaning | define api documentation | api documentation explained simply => API documentation explains each function or endpoint: what it does, what to pass and what it returns, often with examples.
what is pair programming in teams | pair programming in teams meaning | define pair programming in teams | pair programming in teams explained simply => Pair programming means two people work on the same code together, one typing and one reviewing, swapping often.
what is hackathon project tips | what is hackathon tips | hackathon project tips meaning | define hackathon project tips | hackathon project tips explained simply => At a hackathon, pick a small idea, build the core first, keep a working version at all times, and practise a short demo.
what is prototype in software | what is prototyping | prototype in software meaning | define prototype in software | prototype in software explained simply => A prototype is a quick rough version made to test an idea before building it properly.
what is user story | user story meaning | define user story | user story explained simply => A user story describes a feature from the user's view, like 'As a player, I want to save my progress so I can continue later.'
what is bug report | bug report meaning | define bug report | bug report explained simply => A good bug report says what you did, what you expected, what actually happened, and how to make it happen again.
# tag: coding.cs.networks
what is internet | internet meaning | define internet => The internet is a worldwide network of networks that lets computers send data to each other using shared rules called protocols.
what is protocol | protocol meaning | define protocol | protocol explained simply => A protocol is an agreed set of rules for how computers talk, like HTTP for web pages or TCP for reliable delivery.
what is url | url meaning | define url | url explained simply => A URL is a full web address, like https://example.com/page, made of a scheme (https), a domain and a path.
what is https | define https | https explained simply => HTTPS is HTTP encrypted with TLS, so others on the network cannot read or change what you send. Look for it before logging in anywhere.
what is tcp | tcp meaning | define tcp | tcp explained simply => TCP is a protocol that makes sure all data arrives, in order, resending anything lost. Web pages use it.
what is packet | packet meaning | define packet | packet explained simply => Data on the internet is cut into small packets that travel separately and are put back together at the other end.
what is router | router meaning | define router | router explained simply => A router sends packets between networks, like between your home WiFi devices and the internet.
what is server | define server | server explained simply => A server is a computer (or program) that provides data or services to other computers, called clients.
what is latency | latency meaning | define latency | latency explained simply => Latency, or ping, is how long data takes to go to a server and back, in milliseconds. Lower ping means less lag in online games.
what is bandwidth | bandwidth meaning | define bandwidth | bandwidth explained simply => Bandwidth is how much data a connection can carry each second, measured in megabits per second (Mbps).
what is cloud computing | cloud computing meaning | define cloud computing | cloud computing explained simply => The cloud means using computers in big data centers over the internet, for storage, games, websites or computing power, instead of your own machine.
what is database | database meaning | define database | database explained simply => A database stores and organizes lots of data so it can be searched and updated quickly, like player profiles or a shop's orders.
what is sql | sql meaning | define sql | sql explained simply => SQL is a language for asking databases questions, like `SELECT name FROM players WHERE score > 100;`.
what is primary key | primary key meaning | define primary key | primary key explained simply => A primary key is a column whose value is unique for every row in a database table, like a player's UserId.
what is public key cryptography | public key cryptography meaning | define public key cryptography | public key cryptography explained simply => Public key cryptography uses a pair of keys: anyone can lock a message with your public key, but only your private key can unlock it.
what is password hashing | password hashing meaning | define password hashing | password hashing explained simply => Websites should store passwords as a slow, salted hash rather than the password itself, so a stolen database does not reveal them.
what is salt in hashing | what is password salt | salt in hashing meaning | define salt in hashing | salt in hashing explained simply => A salt is random data added to each password before hashing, so the same password gives different hashes and precomputed tables do not work.
what is firewall | firewall meaning | define firewall | firewall explained simply => A firewall blocks network traffic that is not allowed, protecting a computer or network from unwanted connections.
what is ddos attack | what is ddos | ddos attack meaning | define ddos attack | ddos attack explained simply => A DDoS attack floods a server with fake traffic from many computers so real users cannot get through. Doing it is illegal.
what is open port | what is port number | open port meaning | define open port | open port explained simply => A port number picks which program on a computer gets network data, like 443 for HTTPS. One IP address can have many ports.
what is localhost | localhost meaning | define localhost | localhost explained simply => The name localhost (127.0.0.1) means your own computer, used to test servers before putting them online.
what is websocket | websocket meaning | define websocket | websocket explained simply => A WebSocket keeps a connection open between a browser and server so both can send messages any time, which is good for chat and live games.
what is cdn | cdn meaning | define cdn | cdn explained simply => A CDN (content delivery network) keeps copies of files on servers around the world so they load fast from somewhere nearby.
what is api key | api key meaning | define api key | api key explained simply => An API key is a secret code that identifies your program to a service. Keep it out of shared code and never post it publicly.
what is rate limit | rate limit meaning | define rate limit | rate limit explained simply => A rate limit caps how many requests you can make in a time period. Going over it gives errors like HTTP 429, so slow down and retry later.
